findings.text: blocking: neither base_gate.log nor head_gate.log carries a command, revision or tree header — both begin with the pytest session banner — while this sprint's working rules require the literal command as a log's first line and the manifest claims each log's first line names the revision, the tree and the command; the 151-passed/155-passed EXIT=0 pair therefore cannot be attributed to a revision from the logs themselves, and the base arm (run from an extracted copy of 033ee2a30) is named only in the manifest's prose. The repair is to re-capture the two logs with the command line, not to re-measure.

follow-on: `removed` (harmonize.py:1096) and `added` (harmonize.py:1108) are accumulated over every present member, before the protection filter at harmonize.py:1136 drops the withheld rows from the write; the returned dict therefore reports changes that were never written. In the protected fixture the step returns removed=1 for the probe's dead `name:base_of_ghost` link while the same test asserts that link is still present in the graph (tests/standard_names/test_harmonize_reverse_links.py:397) — the report says a link was removed, the graph says it was not, which is the partial-write-reads-as-complete class this node set out to repair.

follow-on: the step is invoked per family with that family's members, so it makes links reciprocal only between members of one family, while the report path audits `missing_reverse` over the union of every in-scope family's members (harmonize.py:594, `run_link_integrity(in_scope, known_ids=known_ids)`); a one-way `name:` link between members of two different in-scope families therefore remains a missing_reverse finding the step cannot clear, so the goal's "no sibling link unreturned" holds within a family and not across the report's scope.

follow-on: `_without_the_step` is defined and never called by any test in the file (a search for the name returns only the definition), because the step-removed red run is produced by the out-of-tree plugin red_plugins/red_step_removed.py; the helper that appears to be the mechanism-removal control is unreachable dead code.

follow-on: the brief's second mechanism rule ("a sibling link that should not exist, because it is not a family sibling or the target is not in the catalog, is removed") is implemented only for the second clause — a live `name:` link out of the family is kept, not removed. I judge the landed rule correct and the brief's clause over-broad: the audit reports missing_reverse only for targets inside its scope, and members legitimately carry live cross-family references (the fragment names name:poloidal_magnetic_flux and name:volume_averaged_*_density), so a sibling-only removal would delete valid references to clear a finding the audit would never raise. Recorded because it is a deviation from an exact-node instruction, not because it should be reversed.
